one_month_reasoning: No Adobe-specific scheduled catalyst falls in the 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-30 window: Q3 FY26 was reported 2026-09-10, Q4 FY26 results and the first FY27 guide come ~Dec 9, Adobe MAX is Nov 10-12 and the CEO handover is Dec 1, all after the window (supervisor confirmed). In-window drivers: the Oct 28 FOMC (hike odds fell from ~64% to ~35-37% after the softer August PCE on Sep 30, so some rate risk is already out) and late-October mega-cap/software earnings read-through, both two-sided. Wadhwani's exit took effect Sep 27 and is already public. Short-horizon reversal after the ~18% drop from the early-September high roughly offsets negative post-earnings momentum. So I centre on today's price (median ~$238.5) with ~10.5% one-month sigma (a bit under 41%/3.5 because nothing Adobe-specific is scheduled) plus a modest fat-tail mixture; essentially unchanged from round 1.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (NTM EPS at Sep-2027 ~$29.4 x 9.5x = $279, weight 0.5) and after-SBC FCF yield (Sep-2027 FCF after SBC ~$25.8/share at 9.5% = $272, weight 0.5), giving ~$275. The price-forecast median (~$254) sits below it because my base-rate lane says disruption-scare names re-rate slowly (median return about market-like).

inputs_detail.derivation: Aggregator consensus ~$30.0 (single-source, per supervisor) trimmed ~1% for the reset risk at the first FY27 guide under a new CEO with the core Creative head (Wadhwani) gone and organic ARR growth ~9%; ~2% per-year share shrink from buybacks supports ~7.5% EPS growth over FY27.

Adobe's fiscal year ends late November (Q3 ended Aug 28, 2026), so NTM at 2027-09-30 is ~2/12 FY27 + 10/12 FY28 = (2 x 27.67 + 10 x 29.75)/12 = $29.4. Round 1 used full FY28 $30.5, which was ~3% high.

Today ~8.8x NTM (a 5-year low; 23-25x in early 2024). Sparkline's disruption-scare base rate is a median return about equal to the market, i.e. little systematic re-rating, so I allow only ~0.7 turn of expansion (half the gap I assumed in round 1 with 10x) for buyback support and near-zero net debt.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: TTM CFO $10.81B less capex ~$0.24B less SBC ~$2.1B = ~$8.5B; grown ~8% to ~$9.2B at Sep-2027 over ~362M shares -> ~$25.8/share, capitalized at 9.5%; net debt ~$0.7B immaterial

inputs_detail.derivation: FY25 CFO $10.03B - 9M FY25 $6.871B + 9M FY26 $7.646B (arithmetic confirmed by supervisor from the 8-K and 10-Q).
Q3 SBC annualized; deducted because buybacks mostly offset dilution from it. Round 1 omitted this.
10-Q cover 389.2M; Q3 buyback $2.23B (~9.5M shares) with $24.55B authorization left, net of ~1.5M issued per quarter -> ~7M net retired per quarter x 4 = ~362M. Round 1's 385M was stale.
Debt $6.363B less cash and ST investments $5.639B.
Today's after-SBC yield is ~9.1%; 9.5% assumes no re-rating (slightly wider) consistent with the base rate that disruption-scare names stay cheap; far above Adobe's historical 3-4%.

bear.story: The Dec-9 FY27 guide under a new CEO, an interim CFO and no core Creative head resets expectations: organic ARR growth slips from ~9% toward 6-7% as Q3's -37% net new ARR decline proves a trend, not a blip; Canva/Figma/Google/OpenAI erode seats and pricing. NTM EPS ~$26.5 at ~6.5x = ~$170, below the June-2026 low of $190.

base.story: Adobe grows organic ARR ~8-9% and EPS ~10% with the share count falling to ~362M; the Q4 net new ARR decline narrows to ~-16% as the guide implies, but the market keeps it in the disruption-scare bucket at ~8.8x NTM EPS ~$29.4 = ~$258, a market-like return as the Sparkline base rate suggests.

bull.story: Chakravarthy's first guide and MAX show credible freemium/agentic monetization, net new ARR stabilizes, software keeps rallying off the April 'SaaSpocalypse' low; multiple re-rates to ~12x NTM EPS ~$29.4 = ~$350, echoing the 2022-23 rebound (+85% in 12 months after the Figma low).

thesis_break_reason: A close near $175 is ~8% under the June-2026 panic low ($190.12) and ~6x NTM EPS with an after-SBC FCF yield near 13%; with cash flow intact the stock has held above $190 through the SaaSpocalypse, so trading there would most likely mean earnings power itself is breaking (organic ARR growth to mid-single digits, a guide-down from the new leadership, net seat losses) rather than 41%-vol noise.

reasoning: Round 2 changes are mostly valuation hygiene from the supervisor: (1) NTM EPS at Sep-2027 uses Adobe's late-November fiscal year, ~$29.4 not $30.5; (2) FCF is after ~$2.1B SBC and on ~362M Sep-2027 shares (10-Q cover 389.2M, ~7M net retired per quarter), not pre-SBC on a stale 385M; (3) I cut the P/E multiple to 9.5x from 10x so the fundamental value is consistent with my own base-rate lane. Fair value falls from $300 to ~$275. New facts that lower the left side: Q3 net new ARR fell ~37% y/y and is essentially organic (organic ARR growth ~9%), and the 8-K (verified) confirms Wadhwani, President of Creativity & Productivity, left effective Sep 27, leaving the core business without its head before the Dec-9 guide. The FY guide implying Q4 net new ARR only ~-16% y/y is a partial offset. Base rates (my lane): Sparkline's disruption-scare cohort has a median 12-month return about equal to the market with ~1.8x wider dispersion; so I keep the median near ~$254 (flat ~8.8x on NTM EPS ~$29.4 = $258, trimmed slightly for the leadership gap), effective sigma ~0.37-0.40 with a fat-tail mixture. On the supervisor's challenge to my right tail: Sparkline's ~10% doubling rate refers to touching 2x within a year, not closing there on a fixed date, and the organic slowdown weakens the re-rating case, so I trim P(>=476) from 6.1% to 4.7% and P(>=595) from 2.2% to 1.4%; I keep a real right tail because the stock is at a 5-year-low multiple with ~9% after-SBC FCF yield and Adobe rose ~85% in the year after its 2022 low. Scenario mean ~$259; P(>= spot) 0.56. Polymarket recession odds: verified the market exists at ~35% but volume is only ~$9.6K, so I treat it as weak colour, not an input. Research in round 2 was limited to two searches.
